scope: Functional McKernel OS/apps and Rust/assembly migration only; no security testing.
change: On the selected entry-only counter allocator failure, release the fresh event with its matching provider and return the same negative result. No successful-path change.
assumptions: The paired current x86 perf counter provider only scans thread pmc_alloc_map and publishes no event reference or counter reservation.
The selected event allocator returns one initialized, live, exclusively owned event; its current hw initializer and mapping providers do not publish that pointer.
The callback is called only after successful allocation and before group linkage, host offload, pmc map update or fd publication; selected matching free bridge consumes the event exactly once.
The paired C/Rust selection and function pointer ABI must be reviewed and verified in a reviewed actual build before integration.
untouched: No cleanup after group linkage, Linux fd acquisition, or uncertain host completion; no held request work.
verification: Source construction only; no tests, compiler or runtime executed. Independent ownership review required.

required: actual matching f03_perf_allocation_binding_v1 and Rust x86 provider symbols
binding.evidence: syscall_policy.rs event allocator initializes only event-owned data and publishes its pointer to local output; chosen current hw_perf_event_init does not publish. Chosen x86 counter allocator scans thread pmc_alloc_map, returns index or negative without writing map; group setup and host FD call occur only after nonnegative counter result. F03 perf free bridge uses original tracked allocator release.
